newsitem.title: USA: Snyder's departure not seen hurting Gateway.
newsitem.headline: Snyder's departure not seen hurting Gateway.

text.p: The departure of Gateway 2000 Inc President Richard Snyder was not seen as a major blow to the company, whose founder and visionary Ted Waitt was expected to temporarily assume more responsibility at the PC company, an analyst said Monday.
"I don't perceive it as a negative," said Kimberly Alexy of Lehman Brothers. "Ted has always been the visionary" at the PC maker.
Earlier Gateway said Synder, who also is chief operating officer, was leaving to lead an entrepreneurial private venture capital fund to be headquartered near Ann Arbor, Mich.
Gateway has launched a search for a successor.

Last week, Gateway reported earnings of $56.5 million, or $0.36 a share, for the second quarter compared to $51.4 million, or $0.33 a share, in the same period last year. Revenue rose 23 percent to $1.39 billion.
The results met Wall Street's expectations, but analysts said they were concerned about problems with the company's inventories.
"There are some short-term obstacles they have to overcome" in the third quarter, Alexy said.
Gateway's shares fell 11/16 to 39-11/16 on the New York Stock Exchange Monday.
